overview: Newquay Zoo is a compact zoo set in 13 acres of subtropical gardens inside Trenance Leisure Park, about ten minutes’ walk from Newquay railway station. It opened in 1969 and is the largest zoo in Cornwall, with several hundred animals from dozens of species, including some of the world’s rarest small carnivores.
Most families spend two to three hours here. Paths wind between the enclosures and planting, and there are keeper talks, play areas and a few indoor houses to duck into if a shower comes over.

expect.title: Animals
expect.text: Expect penguins, red pandas, primates, tropical birds and reptiles alongside less familiar threatened species, and new arrivals as the zoo develops.

expect.title: Indoor houses
expect.text: Gems of the Jungle is a walk-through space with free-flying tropical birds, and the Tropical House is a warm stop on a cold day.

expect.title: Talks and feeds
expect.text: Keeper talks and feeding times run through the day and are included in the ticket, as are the play areas.

goodToKnow.label: Opening
goodToKnow.text: Open every day from 10am, all year; closing time changes with the season and last entry is an hour before closing.

goodToKnow.label: Tickets
goodToKnow.text: Entry is paid. Online tickets are 15% cheaper as long as you buy them by 10am on the day you go. There are no set family tickets: you choose adult and child tickets individually. Annual memberships are available, including joint ones with Paignton Zoo.

goodToKnow.label: Food
goodToKnow.text: Café Lemur and two seasonal outlets sell meals, snacks and ice cream, and you’re welcome to bring a picnic. Keep an eye on your food: the local gulls are bold.

goodToKnow.label: Getting there
goodToKnow.text: The zoo is within Trenance Leisure Park, close to the town centre and a short walk from the station.

entry.note: Paid entry; tickets online or at the gate
